tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session

- **Save:** hold SAVE and press one of the 16 leftmost keys (KEY1 to
  KEY16, lower and raised keys counted left to right, HW-37): the patch
  playing now is
  saved to that user slot, with the algorithm ALGORITHM chose and the
  mode SEL with MONO or POLY chose; no note plays while SAVE is held. The
  screen's event line says "saved to slot n" (or "SAVE FAILED, slot n").
  KNOB1 to KNOB4 stay offsets over the patch, as they are over every
  patch, and are not saved, so a saved patch never takes them twice.
  The program stays as it was.
- **Programs:** PRESETS and program changes reach the test patches (0 to
  8), then the user slots that hold a patch (9 to 24). With no user
  slots, PRESETS turns as before.
- **Factory defaults:** hold SAVE and HOME together for 2 s: every user
  slot empty, the settings' defaults, the first program; the event line
  says "factory defaults". Held less, nothing happens.
- **Kept without asking:** the selection and the settings, once they have
  stayed changed for 2 s (above).

128:| R-STORE-1 | The store (M7) is our own design (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M7; docs/STORE-FORMAT.md) since M8a in the stock layout's unused region, chip offsets `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF` (HW-80; one definition; M7 used the stock user patch region, `0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`), clear of the boot area, the Bluetooth sector, the stock firmware's user patch region and the per-unit last sector; the image is linked to end before the user patch region, and no run of the store's tests changes the chip outside the store but for fwtest's own image (persist and wear start with the user patch region full of a pattern, which they leave unchanged). tools/store.py reads and writes the same format, and its constants are the firmware's. | M7 | C-UNIT, C-FW-SUITE |
129:| R-STORE-2 | What is kept: the user slots (16, each a patch in docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md's format), the patch selection, and `struct midi_settings` (the receive and send channels, bend range, controller map, thru, local control). 130:| R-STORE-3 | Power cuts: records carry a kind, an id, a version, a length, a sequence number and a CRC-32; a write never changes a written byte, so the previous good copy stays readable until the new one is complete. #!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The preset bank's tests (M8b, a draft; docs/M8-PROPOSAL.md, "Presets"):
every preset in tools/fm_patch.py's PRESETS played in fwtest by the
shipping image, through MIDI in: a program change, a reference note (C4
at velocity 100, held 2 s, then 1 s to fade), then a short phrase (C4 E4
G4 C5, then the C major chord held 1 s). Four runs at a time.

  preset_suite.py --image APP.bin --out DIR [--drop DIR] [--write-golden]

Each reference note is checked:
- no clipping (no sample at 16-bit full scale) and no DC (the held note's
  mean under 0.5% of full scale);
- no click: the note's first sample under 5% of its peak (no jump from
  silence), and no step in the 5 ms after the note off more than twice
  the largest in the 5 ms before it;
- its loudness (the RMS of its loudest 20 ms) within 3 dB of the bank's
  target (TARGET_DB), so the bank plays at one level;
- its category's shape: a bass has most of its power below 300 Hz, a pad
  takes 50 ms or more to reach 3 dB under its peak, a pluck falls 30 dB
  within 2 s while held;
- on all 16 voices (a 16-note chord, 500 ms): no underrun, every block
  filled within its 1 451 us;
- the WAV against its SHA-256 in tests/fw/golden/presets.json (fwtest is
  exact), unless --write-golden writes them: the SHA-256 of its first
  HASH_FRAMES frames, whole blocks that end at least 2 ms before RUN_MS.
  The WAV ends when the run does, and a run that ends while core 0 waits
  ends late (docs/HARNESS.md, "Time"), by an amount that moves with core
  0's instruction count (fwtest 0.6.0's flash busy time moved P44's and
  P47's by a block), so the frames after that are left out.
tools/fw-suite.py runs it after the store's cases (run()), since M8b.
With --drop, each run's WAV is copied there as NN-name.wav, with
INDEX.md (number, name, category, what it is for, its loudness).
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import audio_analysis as aa  # noqa: E402  (tools/, our own)
import fm_patch  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
GOLDEN = os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "golden", "presets.json")
FIRST_PROGRAM = 25          # fm.h: FM_PRESET0
TARGET_DB = -25.0           # dBFS RMS of each reference note's loudest 20 ms
TOLERANCE_DB = 3.0
NOTE_ON_MS, NOTE_OFF_MS, RUN_MS = 300, 2300, 6200
FULL = 32767
HASH_FRAMES = int((RUN_MS - 2) * aa.RATE / 1000) // 64 * 64   # 273 408


def script(program):
    lines = ["100 midi c0 %02x" % program, "%d midi 90 3c 64" % NOTE_ON_MS, "%d midi 80 3c 00" % NOTE_OFF_MS]
    t = 3300
    for note in (0x3C, 0x40, 0x43, 0x48):
        lines += ["%d midi 90 %02x 64" % (t, note), "%d midi 80 %02x 00" % (t + 230, note)]
        t += 250
    lines += ["4400 midi 90 3c 64 90 40 64 90 43 64", "5400 midi 80 3c 00 80 40 00 80 43 00"]
    return lines


def chord_script(program):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

"""The preset bank's tests (M8b, a draft; docs/M8-PROPOSAL.md, "Presets"):
every preset in tools/fm_patch.py's PRESETS played in fwtest by the
shipping image, through MIDI in: a program change, a reference note (C4
at velocity 100, held 2 s, then 1 s to fade), then a short phrase (C4 E4
G4 C5, then the C major chord held 1 s). Four runs at a time.

  preset_suite.py --image APP.bin --out DIR [--drop DIR] [--write-golden]

Each reference note is checked:
- no clipping (no sample at 16-bit full scale) and no DC (the held note's
  mean under 0.5% of full scale);
- no click: the note's first sample under 5% of its peak (no jump from
  silence), and no step in the 5 ms after the note off more than twice
  the largest in the 5 ms before it;
- its loudness (the RMS of its loudest 20 ms) within 3 dB of the bank's
  target (TARGET_DB), so the bank plays at one level;
- its category's shape: a bass has most of its power below 300 Hz, a pad
  takes 50 ms or more to reach 3 dB under its peak, a pluck falls 30 dB
  within 2 s while held;
- on all 16 voices (a 16-note chord, 500 ms): no underrun, every block
  filled within its 1 451 us;
- the WAV against its SHA-256 in tests/fw/golden/presets.json (fwtest is
  exact), unless --write-golden writes them: the SHA-256 of its first
  HASH_FRAMES frames, whole blocks that end at least 2 ms before RUN_MS.
  The WAV ends when the run does, and a run that ends while core 0 waits
  ends late (docs/HARNESS.md, "Time"), by an amount that moves with core
  0's instruction count (fwtest 0.6.0's flash busy time moved P44's and
  P47's by a block), so the frames after that are left out.
tools/fw-suite.py runs it after the store's cases (run()), since M8b.
With --drop, each run's WAV is copied there as NN-name.wav, with
INDEX.md (number, name, category, what it is for, its loudness).
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import audio_analysis as aa  # noqa: E402  (tools/, our own)
import fm_patch  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
GOLDEN = os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "golden", "presets.json")
FIRST_PROGRAM = 25          # fm.h: FM_PRESET0
TARGET_DB = -25.0           # dBFS RMS of each reference note's loudest 20 ms
TOLERANCE_DB = 3.0
NOTE_ON_MS, NOTE_OFF_MS, RUN_MS = 300, 2300, 6200
FULL = 32767
HASH_FRAMES = int((RUN_MS - 2) * aa.RATE / 1000) // 64 * 64   # 273 408


def script(program):
    lines = ["100 midi c0 %02x" % program, "%d midi 90 3c 64" % NOTE_ON_MS, "%d midi 80 3c 00" % NOTE_OFF_MS]
    t = 3300
    for note in (0x3C, 0x40, 0x43, 0x48):
        lines += ["%d midi 90 %02x 64" % (t, note), "%d midi 80 %02x 00" % (t + 230, note)]
        t += 250
    lines += ["4400 midi 90 3c 64 90 40 64 90 43 64", "5400 midi 80 3c 00 80 40 00 80 43 00"]
    return lines


def chord_script(program):
    """All 16 voices: 16 notes at once, C3 up a whole tone at a time."""
    notes = " ".join("90 %02x 64" % (48 + 2 * k) for k in range(16))
    return ["100 midi c0 %02x" % program, "300 midi " + notes]


def rel(path):
    return os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)

AUDIO_RAM = "0x01c00550:0x40@end"   # the audio record (audio.h): blocks, underruns, fill_max at words 2, 3, 5
BLOCK_TICKS = 34816                   # a block, 64 frames of 544 time base ticks


def load(image, out, i):
    """Preset i on all 16 voices for 500 ms: (underruns, the longest fill
    in time base ticks)."""
    d = os.path.join(out, "c%02d" % (i + 1))
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    s = os.path.join(out, "c%02d.txt" % (i + 1))
    with open(s, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(chord_script(FIRST_PROGRAM + i)) + "\n")
    subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", rel(image), "--ms", "800", "--script", rel(s), "--ram", AUDIO_RAM,
                    "--out", rel(d)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "ram-01c00550-40-end.bin"), "rb") as f:
        w = struct.unpack("<16I", f.read()[:64])
    return w[3], w[5]


def render(image, out, i):
    """Runs preset i; returns the WAV's path, or raises."""
    d = os.path.join(out, "p%02d" % (i + 1))
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    s = os.path.join(out, "p%02d.txt" % (i + 1))
    with open(s, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(script(FIRST_PROGRAM + i)) + "\n")
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", rel(image), "--ms", str(RUN_MS), "--script", rel(s), "--wav",
                        "--out", rel(d)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    wav = os.path.join(d, "audio.wav")
    if p.returncode or not os.path.exists(wav):
        raise RuntimeError("preset %d: fwtest: %s" % (i + 1, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-300:]))
    return wav


def sound_sha256(wav):
    """The SHA-256 of the WAV's first HASH_FRAMES frames (16-bit stereo)."""
    with open(wav, "rb") as f:
        b = f.read()
    i = 12
    while b[i:i + 4] != b"data":
        i += 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]
    data = b[i + 8:i + 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]]
    if len(data) < HASH_FRAMES * 4:
        raise ValueError("%s: %d frames, fewer than %d" % (rel(wav), len(data) // 4, HASH_FRAMES))
    return hashlib.sha256(data[:HASH_FRAMES * 4]).hexdigest()


def db(x):
    return 20 * math.log10(x / FULL) if x > 0 else -200.0


def measure(wav):
    """The reference note's figures."""
    rate, x, _ = aa.read_wav(wav)
    r = aa.RATE
    on, off = int(NOTE_ON_MS * r / 1000), int(NOTE_OFF_MS * r / 1000)
    start = on
    while start < off and not x[start]:
        start += 1
    note = x[start:off + int(1.0 * r)]
    held = x[start:off]
    win = int(0.02 * r)
    step = int(0.005 * r)
    loud = max(math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in held[k:k + win]) / win) for k in range(0, max(1, len(held) - win), step))
    peak = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 0
    mean = sum(held) / len(held) if held else 0
    # A click: the note starting with a jump from silence (its first
    # sample over 5% of its peak), or a step in the 5 ms after the note off
    # more than twice the largest in the 5 ms before it.
    def steps(a, b):
        return max([abs(x[n] - x[n - 1]) for n in range(max(a, 1), b)] or [0])
    ms5 = int(0.005 * r)
    peak_note = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 1
    jump = max(20 * abs(x[start]) / max(1, peak_note), steps(off, off + ms5) / max(1, steps(off - ms5, off)))
    env = aa.envelope(held, 64)
    top = max(env) if env else 0
    attack = aa.attack_ms(held, 0) if top else 0
    after2s = max(env[-int(0.1 * r / 64):]) if env else 0
    low = 1 - aa.share_above(held[:8192], 300.0) if len(held) >= 8192 else 0
    return {"loud_db": db(loud), "peak": peak, "dc": abs(mean) / FULL, "jump": jump, "attack_ms": attack,
            "fall_db": db(after2s) - db(top), "low_share": low}


def check(i, m):
    category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
    problems = []
    if m["peak"] >= FULL:
        problems.append("clips")
    if m["dc"] > 0.005:
        problems.append("DC %.3f" % m["dc"])
    if m["jump"] > 2:
        problems.append("a click at the note's edge (%.1f, where 2 is the limit)" % m["jump"])
    if abs(m["loud_db"] - TARGET_DB) > TOLERANCE_DB:
        problems.append("loudness %.1f dBFS, the target %.1f +- %.0f" % (m["loud_db"], TARGET_DB, TOLERANCE_DB))
    if category == 1 and m["low_share"] < 0.5:
        problems.append("a bass with %.0f%% of its power below 300 Hz" % (100 * m["low_share"]))
    if category == 4 and m["attack_ms"] < 50:
        problems.append("a pad whose attack takes %.0f ms" % m["attack_ms"])
    if category == 6 and m["fall_db"] > -30:
        problems.append("a pluck that falls only %.0f dB in 2 s" % -m["fall_db"])
    return problems


def run(image, out, which=None, write_golden=False):
    """Plays and checks presets `which` (indexes; all by default):
    (problems, rows, wavs, sums), printing a line for each."""
    which = range(len(fm_patch.PRESETS)) if which is None else which
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
        wavs = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: render(image, out, i), which)))
        loads = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: load(image, out, i), which)))
    golden = {}
    if os.path.exists(GOLDEN):
        with open(GOLDEN) as f:
            golden = json.load(f)
    problems, rows, sums = [], [], {}
    for i in which:
        category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
        m = measure(wavs[i])
        sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)] = sound_sha256(wavs[i])
        more = check(i, m)
        under, fill = loads[i]
        m["fill_us"] = fill / 24.0
        if under or fill >= BLOCK_TICKS:
            more.append("on 16 voices: %d underruns, the longest fill %.0f us" % (under, fill / 24.0))
        if not write_golden and golden.get("P%02d" % (i + 1)) != sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)]:
            more.append("the WAV differs from its golden SHA-256" if "P%02d" % (i + 1) in golden
                        else "no golden SHA-256")
        problems += ["P%02d %s: %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], q) for q in more]
        rows.append((i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], purpose, m))
        print("P%02d %-12s %-22s %6.1f dBFS  attack %6.1f ms  2 s %6.1f dB  below 300 Hz %3.0f%%  16 voices %4.0f us"
              "  %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], m["loud_db"], m["attack_ms"], m["fall_db"],
                        100 * m["low_share"], m["fill_us"], "PASS" if not more else "FAIL"))
    return problems, rows, wavs, sums


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--image", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--drop")
    ap.add_argument("--write-golden", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--only", type=int, nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--calibrate", action="store_true",
                    help="rewrite tools/fm_patch.py's TRIM toward TARGET_DB from this render")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    which = [k - 1 for k in a.only] if a.only else None
    problems, rows, wavs, sums = run(a.image, out, which, a.write_golden)
    if a.calibrate:
        trims = dict(fm_patch.TRIM)
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            steps = round((TARGET_DB - m["loud_db"]) / (48.16 / 64))
            trims[name] = trims.get(name, 0) + steps
        trims = {k: v for k, v in sorted(trims.items()) if v}
        path = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "fm_patch.py")
        with open(path) as f:
            src = f.read()
        i = src.index("TRIM = {")
        j = src.index("}", i) + 1
        body = ",\n        ".join("%r: %d" % kv for kv in trims.items())
        src = src[:i] + "TRIM = {\n        " + body + ",\n}" + src[j:] if trims else src[:i] + "TRIM = {}" + src[j:]
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(src)
        print("calibrate: TRIM rewritten for %d presets" % len(trims))
    if a.write_golden:
        with open(GOLDEN, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"comment": "SHA-256 of each preset's run in tools/preset_suite.py (its WAV's first"
                                  " HASH_FRAMES frames)",
                       **sums}, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            f.write("\n")
    if a.drop:
        os.makedirs(a.drop, exist_ok=True)
        idx = ["# The preset bank (M8b, a draft): what to listen to", "",
               "Each WAV: a program change, then C4 held 2 s (the reference note) and 1 s to fade, then C4 E4 G4"
               " C5 and the C major chord held 1 s. Rendered by fwtest from the image the draft pull request"
               " builds; loudness is the reference note's loudest 20 ms.", "",
               "| # | Name | Category | What it is for | Loudness |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            fn = "%02d-%s.wav" % (n, "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "-" for c in name).strip("-").lower())
            shutil.copyfile(wavs[n - 1], os.path.join(a.drop, fn))
            idx.append("| %d | [%s](%s) | %s | %s | %.1f dBFS |" % (n, name, fn, cat, purpose, m["loud_db"]))
        with open(os.path.join(a.drop, "INDEX.md"), "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(idx) + "\n")

AUDIO_RAM = "0x01c00550:0x40@end"   # the audio record (audio.h): blocks, underruns, fill_max at words 2, 3, 5
BLOCK_TICKS = 34816                   # a block, 64 frames of 544 time base ticks


def load(image, out, i):
    """Preset i on all 16 voices for 500 ms: (underruns, the longest fill
    in time base ticks)."""
    d = os.path.join(out, "c%02d" % (i + 1))
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    s = os.path.join(out, "c%02d.txt" % (i + 1))
    with open(s, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(chord_script(FIRST_PROGRAM + i)) + "\n")
    subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", rel(image), "--ms", "800", "--script", rel(s), "--ram", AUDIO_RAM,
                    "--out", rel(d)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "ram-01c00550-40-end.bin"), "rb") as f:
        w = struct.unpack("<16I", f.read()[:64])
    return w[3], w[5]


def render(image, out, i):
    """Runs preset i; returns the WAV's path, or raises."""
    d = os.path.join(out, "p%02d" % (i + 1))
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    s = os.path.join(out, "p%02d.txt" % (i + 1))
    with open(s, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(script(FIRST_PROGRAM + i)) + "\n")
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", rel(image), "--ms", str(RUN_MS), "--script", rel(s), "--wav",
                        "--out", rel(d)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    wav = os.path.join(d, "audio.wav")
    if p.returncode or not os.path.exists(wav):
        raise RuntimeError("preset %d: fwtest: %s" % (i + 1, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-300:]))
    return wav


def sound_sha256(wav):
    """The SHA-256 of the WAV's first HASH_FRAMES frames (16-bit stereo)."""
    with open(wav, "rb") as f:
        b = f.read()
    i = 12
    while b[i:i + 4] != b"data":
        i += 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]
    data = b[i + 8:i + 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]]
    if len(data) < HASH_FRAMES * 4:
        raise ValueError("%s: %d frames, fewer than %d" % (rel(wav), len(data) // 4, HASH_FRAMES))
    return hashlib.sha256(data[:HASH_FRAMES * 4]).hexdigest()


def db(x):
    return 20 * math.log10(x / FULL) if x > 0 else -200.0


def measure(wav):
    """The reference note's figures."""
    rate, x, _ = aa.read_wav(wav)
    r = aa.RATE
    on, off = int(NOTE_ON_MS * r / 1000), int(NOTE_OFF_MS * r / 1000)
    start = on
    while start < off and not x[start]:
        start += 1
    note = x[start:off + int(1.0 * r)]
    held = x[start:off]
    win = int(0.02 * r)
    step = int(0.005 * r)
    loud = max(math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in held[k:k + win]) / win) for k in range(0, max(1, len(held) - win), step))
    peak = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 0
    mean = sum(held) / len(held) if held else 0
    # A click: the note starting with a jump from silence (its first
    # sample over 5% of its peak), or a step in the 5 ms after the note off
    # more than twice the largest in the 5 ms before it.
    def steps(a, b):
        return max([abs(x[n] - x[n - 1]) for n in range(max(a, 1), b)] or [0])
    ms5 = int(0.005 * r)
    peak_note = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 1
    jump = max(20 * abs(x[start]) / max(1, peak_note), steps(off, off + ms5) / max(1, steps(off - ms5, off)))
    env = aa.envelope(held, 64)
    top = max(env) if env else 0
    attack = aa.attack_ms(held, 0) if top else 0
    after2s = max(env[-int(0.1 * r / 64):]) if env else 0
    low = 1 - aa.share_above(held[:8192], 300.0) if len(held) >= 8192 else 0
    return {"loud_db": db(loud), "peak": peak, "dc": abs(mean) / FULL, "jump": jump, "attack_ms": attack,
            "fall_db": db(after2s) - db(top), "low_share": low}


def check(i, m):
    category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
    problems = []
    if m["peak"] >= FULL:
        problems.append("clips")
    if m["dc"] > 0.005:
        problems.append("DC %.3f" % m["dc"])
    if m["jump"] > 2:
        problems.append("a click at the note's edge (%.1f, where 2 is the limit)" % m["jump"])
    if abs(m["loud_db"] - TARGET_DB) > TOLERANCE_DB:
        problems.append("loudness %.1f dBFS, the target %.1f +- %.0f" % (m["loud_db"], TARGET_DB, TOLERANCE_DB))
    if category == 1 and m["low_share"] < 0.5:
        problems.append("a bass with %.0f%% of its power below 300 Hz" % (100 * m["low_share"]))
    if category == 4 and m["attack_ms"] < 50:
        problems.append("a pad whose attack takes %.0f ms" % m["attack_ms"])
    if category == 6 and m["fall_db"] > -30:
        problems.append("a pluck that falls only %.0f dB in 2 s" % -m["fall_db"])
    return problems


def run(image, out, which=None, write_golden=False):
    """Plays and checks presets `which` (indexes; all by default):
    (problems, rows, wavs, sums), printing a line for each."""
    which = range(len(fm_patch.PRESETS)) if which is None else which
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
        wavs = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: render(image, out, i), which)))
        loads = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: load(image, out, i), which)))
    golden = {}
    if os.path.exists(GOLDEN):
        with open(GOLDEN) as f:
            golden = json.load(f)
    problems, rows, sums = [], [], {}
    for i in which:
        category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
        m = measure(wavs[i])
        sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)] = sound_sha256(wavs[i])
        more = check(i, m)
        under, fill = loads[i]
        m["fill_us"] = fill / 24.0
        if under or fill >= BLOCK_TICKS:
            more.append("on 16 voices: %d underruns, the longest fill %.0f us" % (under, fill / 24.0))
        if not write_golden and golden.get("P%02d" % (i + 1)) != sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)]:
            more.append("the WAV differs from its golden SHA-256" if "P%02d" % (i + 1) in golden
                        else "no golden SHA-256")
        problems += ["P%02d %s: %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], q) for q in more]
        rows.append((i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], purpose, m))
        print("P%02d %-12s %-22s %6.1f dBFS  attack %6.1f ms  2 s %6.1f dB  below 300 Hz %3.0f%%  16 voices %4.0f us"
              "  %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], m["loud_db"], m["attack_ms"], m["fall_db"],
                        100 * m["low_share"], m["fill_us"], "PASS" if not more else "FAIL"))
    return problems, rows, wavs, sums


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--image", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--drop")
    ap.add_argument("--write-golden", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--only", type=int, nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--calibrate", action="store_true",
                    help="rewrite tools/fm_patch.py's TRIM toward TARGET_DB from this render")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    which = [k - 1 for k in a.only] if a.only else None
    problems, rows, wavs, sums = run(a.image, out, which, a.write_golden)
    if a.calibrate:
        trims = dict(fm_patch.TRIM)
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            steps = round((TARGET_DB - m["loud_db"]) / (48.16 / 64))
            trims[name] = trims.get(name, 0) + steps
        trims = {k: v for k, v in sorted(trims.items()) if v}
        path = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "fm_patch.py")
        with open(path) as f:
            src = f.read()
        i = src.index("TRIM = {")
        j = src.index("}", i) + 1
        body = ",\n        ".join("%r: %d" % kv for kv in trims.items())
        src = src[:i] + "TRIM = {\n        " + body + ",\n}" + src[j:] if trims else src[:i] + "TRIM = {}" + src[j:]
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(src)
        print("calibrate: TRIM rewritten for %d presets" % len(trims))
    if a.write_golden:
        with open(GOLDEN, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"comment": "SHA-256 of each preset's run in tools/preset_suite.py (its WAV's first"
                                  " HASH_FRAMES frames)",
                       **sums}, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            f.write("\n")
    if a.drop:
        os.makedirs(a.drop, exist_ok=True)
        idx = ["# The preset bank (M8b, a draft): what to listen to", "",
               "Each WAV: a program change, then C4 held 2 s (the reference note) and 1 s to fade, then C4 E4 G4"
               " C5 and the C major chord held 1 s. Rendered by fwtest from the image the draft pull request"
               " builds; loudness is the reference note's loudest 20 ms.", "",
               "| # | Name | Category | What it is for | Loudness |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            fn = "%02d-%s.wav" % (n, "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "-" for c in name).strip("-").lower())
            shutil.copyfile(wavs[n - 1], os.path.join(a.drop, fn))
            idx.append("| %d | [%s](%s) | %s | %s | %.1f dBFS |" % (n, name, fn, cat, purpose, m["loud_db"]))
        with open(os.path.join(a.drop, "INDEX.md"), "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(idx) + "\n")
    for q in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + q)
    print("presets: %d of %d pass" % (len(rows) - len({q.split(":")[0] for q in problems}), len(rows)))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    in time base ticks)."""
    d = os.path.join(out, "c%02d" % (i + 1))

    with open(s, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(script(FIRST_PROGRAM + i)) + "\n")
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", rel(image), "--ms", str(RUN_MS), "--script", rel(s), "--wav",
                        "--out", rel(d)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    wav = os.path.join(d, "audio.wav")
    if p.returncode or not os.path.exists(wav):
        raise RuntimeError("preset %d: fwtest: %s" % (i + 1, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-300:]))
    return wav


def sound_sha256(wav):
    """The SHA-256 of the WAV's first HASH_FRAMES frames (16-bit stereo)."""
    with open(wav, "rb") as f:
        b = f.read()
    i = 12
    while b[i:i + 4] != b"data":
        i += 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]
    data = b[i + 8:i + 8 + struct.unpack("<I", b[i + 4:i + 8])[0]]
    if len(data) < HASH_FRAMES * 4:
        raise ValueError("%s: %d frames, fewer than %d" % (rel(wav), len(data) // 4, HASH_FRAMES))
    return hashlib.sha256(data[:HASH_FRAMES * 4]).hexdigest()


def db(x):
    return 20 * math.log10(x / FULL) if x > 0 else -200.0


def measure(wav):
    """The reference note's figures."""
    rate, x, _ = aa.read_wav(wav)
    r = aa.RATE
    on, off = int(NOTE_ON_MS * r / 1000), int(NOTE_OFF_MS * r / 1000)
    start = on
    while start < off and not x[start]:
        start += 1
    note = x[start:off + int(1.0 * r)]
    held = x[start:off]
    win = int(0.02 * r)
    step = int(0.005 * r)
    loud = max(math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in held[k:k + win]) / win) for k in range(0, max(1, len(held) - win), step))
    peak = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 0
    mean = sum(held) / len(held) if held else 0
    # A click: the note starting with a jump from silence (its first
    # sample over 5% of its peak), or a step in the 5 ms after the note off
    # more than twice the largest in the 5 ms before it.
    def steps(a, b):
        return max([abs(x[n] - x[n - 1]) for n in range(max(a, 1), b)] or [0])
    ms5 = int(0.005 * r)
    peak_note = max(abs(v) for v in note) if note else 1
    jump = max(20 * abs(x[start]) / max(1, peak_note), steps(off, off + ms5) / max(1, steps(off - ms5, off)))
    env = aa.envelope(held, 64)
    top = max(env) if env else 0
    attack = aa.attack_ms(held, 0) if top else 0
    after2s = max(env[-int(0.1 * r / 64):]) if env else 0
    low = 1 - aa.share_above(held[:8192], 300.0) if len(held) >= 8192 else 0
    return {"loud_db": db(loud), "peak": peak, "dc": abs(mean) / FULL, "jump": jump, "attack_ms": attack,
            "fall_db": db(after2s) - db(top), "low_share": low}


def check(i, m):
    category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
    problems = []
    if m["peak"] >= FULL:
        problems.append("clips")
    if m["dc"] > 0.005:
        problems.append("DC %.3f" % m["dc"])
    if m["jump"] > 2:
        problems.append("a click at the note's edge (%.1f, where 2 is the limit)" % m["jump"])
    if abs(m["loud_db"] - TARGET_DB) > TOLERANCE_DB:
        problems.append("loudness %.1f dBFS, the target %.1f +- %.0f" % (m["loud_db"], TARGET_DB, TOLERANCE_DB))
    if category == 1 and m["low_share"] < 0.5:
        problems.append("a bass with %.0f%% of its power below 300 Hz" % (100 * m["low_share"]))
    if category == 4 and m["attack_ms"] < 50:
        problems.append("a pad whose attack takes %.0f ms" % m["attack_ms"])
    if category == 6 and m["fall_db"] > -30:
        problems.append("a pluck that falls only %.0f dB in 2 s" % -m["fall_db"])
    return problems


def run(image, out, which=None, write_golden=False):
    """Plays and checks presets `which` (indexes; all by default):
    (problems, rows, wavs, sums), printing a line for each."""
    which = range(len(fm_patch.PRESETS)) if which is None else which
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
        wavs = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: render(image, out, i), which)))
        loads = dict(zip(which, ex.map(lambda i: load(image, out, i), which)))
    golden = {}
    if os.path.exists(GOLDEN):
        with open(GOLDEN) as f:
            golden = json.load(f)
    problems, rows, sums = [], [], {}
    for i in which:
        category, purpose, p = fm_patch.PRESETS[i]
        m = measure(wavs[i])
        sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)] = sound_sha256(wavs[i])
        more = check(i, m)
        under, fill = loads[i]
        m["fill_us"] = fill / 24.0
        if under or fill >= BLOCK_TICKS:
            more.append("on 16 voices: %d underruns, the longest fill %.0f us" % (under, fill / 24.0))
        if not write_golden and golden.get("P%02d" % (i + 1)) != sums["P%02d" % (i + 1)]:
            more.append("the WAV differs from its golden SHA-256" if "P%02d" % (i + 1) in golden
                        else "no golden SHA-256")
        problems += ["P%02d %s: %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], q) for q in more]
        rows.append((i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], purpose, m))
        print("P%02d %-12s %-22s %6.1f dBFS  attack %6.1f ms  2 s %6.1f dB  below 300 Hz %3.0f%%  16 voices %4.0f us"
              "  %s" % (i + 1, p["name"], fm_patch.CATEGORIES[category], m["loud_db"], m["attack_ms"], m["fall_db"],
                        100 * m["low_share"], m["fill_us"], "PASS" if not more else "FAIL"))
    return problems, rows, wavs, sums


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--image", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--drop")
    ap.add_argument("--write-golden", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--only", type=int, nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--calibrate", action="store_true",
                    help="rewrite tools/fm_patch.py's TRIM toward TARGET_DB from this render")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    which = [k - 1 for k in a.only] if a.only else None
    problems, rows, wavs, sums = run(a.image, out, which, a.write_golden)
    if a.calibrate:
        trims = dict(fm_patch.TRIM)
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            steps = round((TARGET_DB - m["loud_db"]) / (48.16 / 64))
            trims[name] = trims.get(name, 0) + steps
        trims = {k: v for k, v in sorted(trims.items()) if v}
        path = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "fm_patch.py")
        with open(path) as f:
            src = f.read()
        i = src.index("TRIM = {")
        j = src.index("}", i) + 1
        body = ",\n        ".join("%r: %d" % kv for kv in trims.items())
        src = src[:i] + "TRIM = {\n        " + body + ",\n}" + src[j:] if trims else src[:i] + "TRIM = {}" + src[j:]
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(src)
        print("calibrate: TRIM rewritten for %d presets" % len(trims))
    if a.write_golden:
        with open(GOLDEN, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"comment": "SHA-256 of each preset's run in tools/preset_suite.py (its WAV's first"
                                  " HASH_FRAMES frames)",
                       **sums}, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            f.write("\n")
    if a.drop:
        os.makedirs(a.drop, exist_ok=True)
        idx = ["# The preset bank (M8b, a draft): what to listen to", "",
               "Each WAV: a program change, then C4 held 2 s (the reference note) and 1 s to fade, then C4 E4 G4"
               " C5 and the C major chord held 1 s. Rendered by fwtest from the image the draft pull request"
               " builds; loudness is the reference note's loudest 20 ms.", "",
               "| # | Name | Category | What it is for | Loudness |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for n, name, cat, purpose, m in rows:
            fn = "%02d-%s.wav" % (n, "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "-" for c in name).strip("-").lower())
            shutil.copyfile(wavs[n - 1], os.path.join(a.drop, fn))
            idx.append("| %d | [%s](%s) | %s | %s | %.1f dBFS |" % (n, name, fn, cat, purpose, m["loud_db"]))
        with open(os.path.join(a.drop, "INDEX.md"), "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(idx) + "\n")
    for q in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + q)
    print("presets: %d of %d pass" % (len(rows) - len({q.split(":")[0] for q in problems}), len(rows)))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ARP proposal: an arpeggiator on the ARP button

A proposal for the owner to review, written at the end of M8a. Nothing
here is built. The owner answered its questions on 2026-10-25 (recorded
by session owner-answers-1025, at the end); the text above them follows
the answers. It uses only what the firmware and the panel already
offer (HW-36's ARP button and its LED, the engine's note events, MIDI
in and out from M6a and M6b, the screens from M8a) and no new hardware
fact. The owner's answer to the M8 proposal put it next after M8: ARP,
then SEQ (then FX, docs/PLAN.md).

## What it does

While ARP is on, the notes held (on the panel's keys or by MIDI in) are
not played as a chord: the arpeggiator plays them one at a time, in a
pattern, at a rate, over a range of octaves, for as long as they are
held (or latched). Each note it plays is an ordinary note on and note off
to the engine, so every patch, macro and voice rule applies as it does
to a key.

## Modes

| Mode | Order of the held notes |
|---|---|
| UP | lowest to highest, then again |
| DOWN | highest to lowest |
| UP/DOWN | up, then down, the ends not repeated |
| ORDER | the order they were pressed |
| RANDOM | a pseudo-random choice each step (a fixed generator, so a test can predict it) |
| CHORD | all of them together, each step (a rhythmic chord) |

Octaves: 1 to 4. The pattern runs through the held notes, then again an
octave up, up to the range, then starts again.

## Controls

A short press of the ARP button turns the arpeggiator on or off (its LED
lit while on); holding it shows the arpeggiator's screen (answer 3). The
screen
is like EDIT and ENV, with the bottom strip:

| Knob | What | Range |
|---|---|---|
| KNOB1 | RATE | 1/2, dotted 1/4, 1/4, dotted 1/8, 1/8, 1/8T, dotted 1/16, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32 (answer 2) |
| KNOB2 | MODE | the six above |
| KNOB3 | OCTAVES | 1 to 4 |
| KNOB4 | GATE | how long each note sounds: 10% to 100% of its step |

SELECT pages to: SWING (0 to 75%), LATCH (on: notes keep playing after
the keys are let go, until the next chord), TEMPO (40 to 240 BPM, when
the clock is internal), and the MIDI out setting (the arpeggiated notes,
or the keys held; answer 4). The CLOCK page (internal or MIDI) proposed
here is superseded: the arpeggiator follows MIDI clock whenever it
arrives (answer 6).

SEL with a key keeps working as in M8a (operator picks, MONO, POLY).
PRESETS, MASTER, OCT- and OCT+ keep their meanings; OCT moves the notes
the arpeggiator plays as it moves keys.

## Timing

- **The clock:** the engine counts audio blocks (1.451 ms) and samples
  within them, so a step falls on its sample, not on the next block: at
  120 BPM a sixteenth is 125 ms, 5 514.7 frames; the error never grows
  (a fractional accumulator, as the pitch's).
- **MIDI clock in** (0xF8, 24 a beat; Start, Stop, Continue): while MIDI
  clock arrives, each 0xF8 advances the step count by 1/24 of a beat;
  the rate between clocks is smoothed over the last 24 for steps that
  fall between them. When it stops, the internal tempo takes over
  (answer 6). M6a's parser already passes realtime bytes through
  without disturbing other messages.
- **Swing** delays every second step by its share of a step.

## MIDI out

- **The notes the arpeggiator plays go out** as note ons and offs on the
  out channel, so another instrument follows it; the keys held are not
  sent (they are its input, not notes). A setting sends the keys held
  instead (answer 4).
- **MIDI clock out**: when the clock is internal, 0xF8 24 times a beat
  and Start and Stop with the ARP button; when it follows MIDI clock, no
  clock out (thru passes it on if thru is on).
- Local control off: the arpeggiator still runs and its notes go out;
  the engine plays nothing (M6b's rule).

## What it costs

- **CPU:** a step is a few hundred instructions (choose a note, a note
  off for the last, a note on), at most 32 a second at 1/32 and 240 BPM
  with CHORD's notes, so under 0.1% of core 0; the clock is a few
  instructions a block.
- **RAM:** the held notes (up to 16, in pressed order and sorted), the
  pattern's place, the settings: under 100 bytes.
- **Settings:** the arpeggiator's settings are saved with each patch
  (answer 5); how the patch format carries them is the firmware side's
  design (docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md, docs/STORE-FORMAT.md).
- **Screen:** the ARP screen is drawn as the others (M8a's parts); a
  live part shows the step's note.

## Tests

- Each mode's order for a known chord, from MIDI out's capture (exact).
- The steps' timing: each note on's first byte within a block of its
  ideal time at several tempos, and no drift over a minute.
- MIDI clock in at 120 and 90 BPM: the steps follow; Start, Stop and
  Continue; the internal tempo takes over when the clock stops.
- Latch, octaves, gate (each note off at its share of the step), swing.
- Local control off: notes out, nothing played; ARP off: every note it
  started ends.
- Costs: the loaded measure with the arpeggiator at its fastest.

## The owner's answers (2026-10-25)

The questions were:

1. **Modes:** the six above, or fewer (UP, DOWN, UP/DOWN, RANDOM) to
   start?
2. **Rates:** the six divisions, or also whole notes, halves and
   dotted ones?
3. **The ARP button:** short press on or off, and hold it to show the ARP
   screen (as GLO shows the settings)? Or press for the screen and turn
   it on there?
4. **MIDI out:** send the arpeggiated notes (as proposed), the keys held,
   or a setting to choose?
5. **Keeping it:** the arpeggiator's settings saved with the other
   settings (one per instrument), or with each patch?
6. **Clock:** follow MIDI clock automatically when it arrives, or only
   when the setting says so?

The owner's answers (recorded by session owner-answers-1025,
docs/prompts/owner-answers-1025.md):

1. **Modes:** all six: UP, DOWN, UP/DOWN, ORDER, RANDOM, CHORD.
2. **Rates:** 1/2, dotted 1/4, 1/4, dotted 1/8, 1/8, 1/8T, dotted 1/16,
   1/16, 1/16T, 1/32. No whole notes.
3. **The ARP button:** a short press turns the arpeggiator on or off;
   holding it shows the ARP screen.
4. **MIDI out:** the arpeggiated notes by default, with a setting to send
   the keys held instead.
5. **Keeping it:** the arpeggiator's settings are saved with each patch.
6. **Clock:** follow incoming MIDI clock automatically, falling back to
   the internal tempo when it stops.

Left to the firmware side's design, and open until it proposes them:

- **When the clock has stopped.** A MIDI Stop, a silence with no 0xF8
  (and how long), or both; and what a Start, a Stop or a Continue does
  to the pattern and to notes still sounding.
- **Moving between the two clocks.** Whether the internal tempo, when it
  takes over, starts from the MIDI clock's last tempo or from the
  patch's TEMPO; and where in the step the pattern carries on.
- **Per patch.** Which settings travel with a patch (on or off, LATCH,
  TEMPO, the MIDI out setting) and which stay with the instrument;
  presets saved before ARP get the defaults.

It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `~/.claude/projects/-HOME-Development-[REDACTED:private]-clean/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Background Session

This session runs as a background job. The user may be chatting with you live or may have stepped away to check results later — respond naturally either way, and don't refer to yourself as "a background agent."

Use `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` (`~/.claude/jobs/cd816ac2/tmp`) for any temporary files (scripts, query files, intermediate outputs) instead of `/tmp` — parallel bg jobs share `/tmp` and clobber each other's files. This directory already exists and is cleaned up when the job is deleted, so anything the user should keep belongs somewhere durable instead.

Edit files directly in your working directory — this session is configured to work in place rather than isolating into a worktree. Skip EnterWorktree unless the user explicitly asks to work in a worktree.

End the job with a report the user can act on: what you did, where it lives — path, branch, PR, or the answer itself — and the next command if one is needed. If you're running as a subagent, the git guidance above and this report don't apply: return your work to your caller.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.
