entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The FM engine's patch format, version 1, and our own test patches
(M5; docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md, R-FM-7).

  fm_patch.py write      writes firmware/src/patches.c from TEST_PATCHES
  fm_patch.py check      exits 1 if firmware/src/patches.c is not what
                         `write` would write, or a patch is not valid

The test patches are defined here, once, in readable units; the firmware
gets them as bytes (patches.c, generated), and tools/fw-suite.py takes
its expected values (levels, times, ratios) from the same definitions.
They are our own: none is, or is derived from, any synthesizer's factory
or published preset.
"""
import os
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "firmware", "src", "patches.c")

BYTES = 112
VERSION = 1
OP_OFFSET, OP_BYTES, SUM_OFFSET = 32, 13, 110
ALGORITHMS = 10
RATIO, FIXED = 0, 1


def time_ms(code):
    """A time code's time: 2^(code / 8) ms (fm.h)."""
    return 2.0 ** (code / 8.0)


def level_gain(level):
    """A level's gain: 2^((level - 127) / 8); 0 is off."""
    return 0.0 if level == 0 else 2.0 ** ((level - 127) / 8.0)


def op(freq, level, mode=RATIO, detune=0, velocity=0, rates=(0, 0, 0, 0), levels=(127, 127, 127)):
    """An operator. freq: a ratio (mode RATIO) or Hz (FIXED)."""
    return {"mode": mode, "freq": freq, "detune": detune, "level": level, "velocity": velocity,
            "rates": tuple(rates), "levels": tuple(levels)}


OFF = op(1.0, 0)


def patch(name, algorithm, ops, feedback=0, mono=False, glide=0, transpose=0,
          pitch_depth=0, pitch_rates=(0, 0, 0), pitch_levels=(0, 0, 0, 0)):
    ops = list(ops) + [OFF] * (6 - len(ops))
    return {"name": name, "algorithm": algorithm, "feedback": feedback, "mono": mono,
            "glide": glide, "transpose": transpose, "pitch_depth": pitch_depth,
            "pitch_rates": tuple(pitch_rates), "pitch_levels": tuple(pitch_levels), "ops": ops}


# The test patches, in PRESETS order. Times are time codes (time_ms),
# levels 0 to 127 (level_gain). Each one is there for a test or to hear
# a kind of sound the algorithms make.
TEST_PATCHES = [
    # 0: one sine carrier at full level, a 5.2 ms attack (linear in
    # amplitude) and a 64 ms release over 96 dB: pitch, level and click
    # tests, and the engine's default.
    patch("Sine", 8, [op(1.0, 127, rates=(19, 0, 0, 48))]),
    # 1: two operators, a modulator at the note's frequency into a carrier
    # at 6 times it, index pi/2 exactly (level 103: a gain of 1/8, of the
    # full scale's 4 pi), flat envelopes: the Bessel test.
    patch("Two-op", 1, [op(6.0, 127, rates=(8, 0, 0, 48)), op(1.0, 103, rates=(8, 0, 0, 48))]),
    # 2: an envelope with every stage: attack 32 ms to 0 dB, decay 1 to
    # level 103 (-18 dB) at 64 ms a 96 dB range, decay 2 to level 87
    # (-30 dB) at 128 ms, release at 256 ms: the envelope timing test.
    patch("Env test", 8, [op(1.0, 127, rates=(40, 48, 56, 64), levels=(127, 103, 87))]),
    # 3: mono, legato, a 181 ms glide: a carrier and one light modulator
    # (index 0.21), so the fundamental's pitch can be followed through the
    # glide: the mono test.
    patch("Glide lead", 1, [op(1.0, 127, rates=(10, 60, 0, 50), levels=(127, 120, 120)),
                            op(1.0, 80, rates=(10, 0, 0, 50))],
          mono=True, glide=60),
    # 4: a struck, inharmonic sound: three pairs, slow decays.
    patch("Bell", 3, [op(1.0, 127, rates=(4, 88, 96, 72), levels=(127, 104, 0)),
                      op(3.5, 100, rates=(4, 80, 90, 72), levels=(127, 96, 0)),
                      op(2.0, 120, detune=7, rates=(4, 84, 92, 72), levels=(127, 100, 0)),
                      op(5.0, 95, rates=(4, 76, 88, 72), levels=(127, 92, 0)),
                      op(3.0, 112, detune=-5, rates=(4, 80, 90, 72), levels=(127, 96, 0)),
                      op(9.2, 90, rates=(4, 72, 84, 72), levels=(127, 90, 0))]),
    # 5: a plucked bass: a three-operator stack and a pair, feedback on
    # the stack's top, fast modulator decays.
    patch("Bass", 9, [op(1.0, 127, rates=(6, 70, 0, 44), levels=(127, 116, 116)),
                      op(1.0, 108, rates=(6, 56, 0, 44), levels=(127, 92, 92)),
                      op(0.5, 120, rates=(6, 0, 0, 44)),
                      op(1.0, 127, rates=(6, 68, 0, 44), levels=(127, 112, 112)),
                      op(1.0, 104, rates=(6, 52, 0, 44), levels=(127, 84, 84)),
                      op(3.0, 96, rates=(6, 48, 0, 44), levels=(127, 80, 80))],
          feedback=5),
    # 6: six carriers at harmonic ratios, an organ-like additive sound;
    # also the heaviest: every operator sounds (the load tests).
    patch("Organ", 8, [op(0.5, 112, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40)), op(1.0, 127, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40)),
                       op(2.0, 116, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40)), op(3.0, 108, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40)),
                       op(4.0, 104, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40)), op(6.0, 100, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40))],
          feedback=2),
    # 7: a brassy stack with a pitch envelope rising a semitone into the
    # note, and velocity sensitivity on every operator: louder and brighter
    # with velocity.
    patch("Brass", 4, [op(1.0, 127, velocity=7, rates=(20, 64, 0, 52), levels=(127, 118, 118)),
                       op(1.0, 108, velocity=7, rates=(24, 64, 0, 52), levels=(127, 104, 104)),
                       op(1.0, 100, velocity=4, rates=(24, 0, 0, 52)),
                       op(2.0, 96, velocity=4, rates=(24, 0, 0, 52)),
                       op(1.0, 98, velocity=4, rates=(24, 0, 0, 52)),
                       op(1.0, 94, velocity=4, rates=(28, 0, 0, 52))],
          feedback=4, pitch_depth=1, pitch_rates=(40, 0, 50), pitch_levels=(-127, 0, 0, 0)),
    # 8: one sine carrier with velocity sensitivity 7 and a flat envelope:
    # the velocity test (its level is the carrier's alone).
    patch("Velocity", 8, [op(1.0, 127, velocity=7, rates=(8, 0, 0, 40))]),
]


def fletcher16(data):
    a = b = 0
    for x in data:
        a = (a + x) % 255
        b = (b + a) % 255
    return b << 8 | a


def encode(p):
    """The patch's FM_PATCH_BYTES bytes (docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md)."""
    b = bytearray(BYTES)
    b[0:4] = bytes((ord("F"), ord("M"), VERSION, BYTES))
    name = p["name"].encode("ascii")
    assert len(name) <= 12 and all(32 <= c < 127 for c in name), p["name"]
    b[4:4 + len(name)] = name
    b[16] = p["algorithm"]
    b[17] = p["feedback"]
    b[18] = 1 if p["mono"] else 0
    b[19] = p["glide"]
    b[20] = p["transpose"] & 0xFF
    b[21] = p["pitch_depth"] & 0xFF
    b[22:25] = bytes(p["pitch_rates"])
    b[25:29] = bytes(v & 0xFF for v in p["pitch_levels"])
    for i, o in enumerate(p["ops"]):
        at = OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * i
        if o["mode"] == RATIO:
            f = int(round(o["freq"] * 256))
        else:
            f = int(round(o["freq"] * 4))
        assert 0 <= f < 65536
        b[at] = o["mode"]
        b[at + 1], b[at + 2] = f & 0xFF, f >> 8
        b[at + 3] = o["detune"] & 0xFF
        b[at + 4] = o["level"]
        b[at + 5] = o["velocity"]
        b[at + 6:at + 10] = bytes(o["rates"])
        b[at + 10:at + 13] = bytes(o["levels"])
    s = fletcher16(b[:SUM_OFFSET])
    b[SUM_OFFSET], b[SUM_OFFSET + 1] = s & 0xFF, s >> 8
    return bytes(b)


def s8(x):
    return x - 256 if x > 127 else x


def problems(b):
    """Why b isn't a valid version 1 patch ([] if it is): the same rules
    as fm_patch_valid() in firmware/src/fm.c."""
    out = []
    if len(b) != BYTES:
        return ["%d bytes, not %d" % (len(b), BYTES)]
    if b[0:4] != bytes((ord("F"), ord("M"), VERSION, BYTES)):
        out.append("header")
    if any(not (c == 0 or 32 <= c < 127) for c in b[4:16]):
        out.append("name")
    if not 1 <= b[16] <= ALGORITHMS:
        out.append("algorithm")
    if b[17] > 7 or b[18] > 1 or b[19] > 127:
        out.append("feedback, flags or glide")
    if not -24 <= s8(b[20]) <= 24 or not -48 <= s8(b[21]) <= 48:
        out.append("transpose or pitch depth")
    if any(x > 127 for x in b[22:25]) or any(s8(x) < -127 for x in b[25:29]) or any(b[29:32]):
        out.append("pitch envelope or reserved")
    for i in range(6):
        o = b[OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * i:OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * (i + 1)]
        if o[0] > 1 or not -100 <= s8(o[3]) <= 100 or o[4] > 127 or o[5] > 7 or any(x > 127 for x in o[6:13]):
            out.append("operator %d" % (i + 1))
    if b[SUM_OFFSET] | b[SUM_OFFSET + 1] << 8 != fletcher16(b[:SUM_OFFSET]):
        out.append("check sum")
    return out


def source():
    lines = ["/*", " * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT", " * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", " *",
             " * The FM engine's test patches, in the patch format's bytes (fm.h,",
             " * docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md). Generated by tools/fm_patch.py from its",
             " * TEST_PATCHES, which says what each one is for: edit those and run",
             " * `tools/fm_patch.py write`, never this file (C-UNIT checks it).", " */", "",
             '#include "fm.h"', "", "const u8 fm_patches[FM_PATCHES][FM_PATCH_BYTES] = {"]
    for i, p in enumerate(TEST_PATCHES):
        b = encode(p)
        lines.append("    /* %d: %s */ {" % (i, p["name"]))
        for k in range(0, BYTES, 16):
            lines.append("        " + " ".join("0x%02x," % x for x in b[k:k + 16]))
        lines.append("    },")
    lines.append("};")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) != 2 or argv[1] not in ("write", "check"):
        print(__doc__.strip().split("\n\n")[1], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    bad = [(i, problems(encode(p))) for i, p in enumerate(TEST_PATCHES)]
    bad = [(i, p) for i, p in bad if p]
    if bad:
        print("invalid test patches: %s" % bad, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if argv[1] == "write":
        with open(OUT, "w") as f:
            f.write(source())
        return 0
    with open(OUT) as f:
        if f.read() != source():
            print("firmware/src/patches.c is not what tools/fm_patch.py writes", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    print("fm patches: %d test patches, valid, patches.c up to date" % len(TEST_PATCHES))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

def fletcher16(data):
    a = b = 0
    for x in data:
        a = (a + x) % 255
        b = (b + a) % 255
    return b << 8 | a


def encode(p):
    """The patch's FM_PATCH_BYTES bytes (docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md)."""
    b = bytearray(BYTES)
    b[0:4] = bytes((ord("F"), ord("M"), VERSION, BYTES))
    name = p["name"].encode("ascii")
    assert len(name) <= 12 and all(32 <= c < 127 for c in name), p["name"]
    b[4:4 + len(name)] = name
    b[16] = p["algorithm"]
    b[17] = p["feedback"]
    b[18] = 1 if p["mono"] else 0
    b[19] = p["glide"]
    b[20] = p["transpose"] & 0xFF
    b[21] = p["pitch_depth"] & 0xFF
    b[22:25] = bytes(p["pitch_rates"])
    b[25:29] = bytes(v & 0xFF for v in p["pitch_levels"])
    for i, o in enumerate(p["ops"]):
        at = OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * i
        if o["mode"] == RATIO:
            f = int(round(o["freq"] * 256))
        else:
            f = int(round(o["freq"] * 4))
        assert 0 <= f < 65536
        b[at] = o["mode"]
        b[at + 1], b[at + 2] = f & 0xFF, f >> 8
        b[at + 3] = o["detune"] & 0xFF
        b[at + 4] = o["level"]
        b[at + 5] = o["velocity"]
        b[at + 6:at + 10] = bytes(o["rates"])
        b[at + 10:at + 13] = bytes(o["levels"])
    s = fletcher16(b[:SUM_OFFSET])
    b[SUM_OFFSET], b[SUM_OFFSET + 1] = s & 0xFF, s >> 8
    return bytes(b)


def s8(x):
    return x - 256 if x > 127 else x


def problems(b):
    """Why b isn't a valid version 1 patch ([] if it is): the same rules
    as fm_patch_valid() in firmware/src/fm.c."""
    out = []
    if len(b) != BYTES:
        return ["%d bytes, not %d" % (len(b), BYTES)]
    if b[0:4] != bytes((ord("F"), ord("M"), VERSION, BYTES)):
        out.append("header")
    if any(not (c == 0 or 32 <= c < 127) for c in b[4:16]):
        out.append("name")
    if not 1 <= b[16] <= ALGORITHMS:
        out.append("algorithm")
    if b[17] > 7 or b[18] > 1 or b[19] > 127:
        out.append("feedback, flags or glide")
    if not -24 <= s8(b[20]) <= 24 or not -48 <= s8(b[21]) <= 48:
        out.append("transpose or pitch depth")
    if any(x > 127 for x in b[22:25]) or any(s8(x) < -127 for x in b[25:29]) or any(b[29:32]):
        out.append("pitch envelope or reserved")
    for i in range(6):
        o = b[OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * i:OP_OFFSET + OP_BYTES * (i + 1)]
        if o[0] > 1 or not -100 <= s8(o[3]) <= 100 or o[4] > 127 or o[5] > 7 or any(x > 127 for x in o[6:13]):
            out.append("operator %d" % (i + 1))
    if b[SUM_OFFSET] | b[SUM_OFFSET + 1] << 8 != fletcher16(b[:SUM_OFFSET]):
        out.append("check sum")
    return out


def source():
    lines = ["/*", " * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT", " * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", " *",
             " * The FM engine's test patches, in the patch format's bytes (fm.h,",
             " * docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md). Generated by tools/fm_patch.py from its",
             " * TEST_PATCHES, which says what each one is for: edit those and run",
             " * `tools/fm_patch.py write`, never this file (C-UNIT checks it).", " */", "",
             '#include "fm.h"', "", "const u8 fm_patches[FM_PATCHES][FM_PATCH_BYTES] = {"]
    for i, p in enumerate(TEST_PATCHES):
        b = encode(p)
        lines.append("    /* %d: %s */ {" % (i, p["name"]))
        for k in range(0, BYTES, 16):
            lines.append("        " + " ".join("0x%02x," % x for x in b[k:k + 16]))
        lines.append("    },")
    lines.append("};")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) != 2 or argv[1] not in ("write", "check"):
        print(__doc__.strip().split("\n\n")[1], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    bad = [(i, problems(encode(p))) for i, p in enumerate(TEST_PATCHES)]
    bad = [(i, p) for i, p in bad if p]
    if bad:
        print("invalid test patches: %s" % bad, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if argv[1] == "write":
        with open(OUT, "w") as f:
            f.write(source())
        return 0
    with open(OUT) as f:
        if f.read() != source():
            print("firmware/src/patches.c is not what tools/fm_patch.py writes", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    print("fm patches: %d test patches, valid, patches.c up to date" % len(TEST_PATCHES))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

# own already makes the compiler use the instructions.
    CPU="-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -DSB_DEMO_PLAITS -Ifirmware/demos/plaits"
    fi
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        build_demo_plaits
    fi
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# presetends (R-MIDIOUT-2, R-STORE-9): PRESETS stops at the ends. From
# the first program (001) with KEY1 held, PRESETS turned down does
# nothing: the note keeps sounding and no program change goes out. Up
# by 30 it stops at the last program that holds a patch (009, with no
# user slots): one program change, 8. Up again from there does nothing.
#
# time   event
200      key 14 down
300      enc 6 -2
500      enc 6 +30
700      key 14 up
900      enc 6 +1
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tests/fw/boot.suite'
s=open(p).read()
i=s.index("midioutlat  ")
j=s.index("\n",i)
line="presetends  completed  ../../out/fw/app.bin           --ms 1100 --script scripts/presetends.txt --midi-out --wav --ipb --console --ram 0x01c00550:0x40@end --ram 0x01c00590:0x40@450 --ram 0x01c00590:0x40@end --ram 0x01c005d0:0x164@end --ram 0x01c00734:0x4c@end --ram 0x01c00000:0x60@end"
s=s[:j+1]+line+"\n"+s[j+1:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='tools/fw-suite.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''"midilocal": "completed", "midiburst": "completed", "midioutlat": "completed",''','''"midilocal": "completed", "midiburst": "completed", "midioutlat": "completed",
          "presetends": "completed",''')
old='''MIDI_CHECKS = {"midimsg": check_midimsg,'''
new='''def check_presetends(case_dir):
    """PRESETS stops at the ends (tests/fw/scripts/presetends.txt): turned
    down from the first program, or up from the last, it does nothing (the
    held note sounds on, no program change goes out); up by 30 from the
    first it stops at the last program that holds a patch."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("presetends", case_dir)
    more, l2, o, msgs, _ = midi_out_common("presetends", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    last = len(fm_patch.TEST_PATCHES) - 1
    problems += expect_messages("presetends", msgs, [(0x90, 53, 100), (0xC0, last), (0x90, 53, 0)], lines)
    f450, f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("450ms"))), fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("end")))
    if (f450["patch"], f450["voices0"] + f450["voices1"], f["patch"], f["notes"]) != (0, 1, last, 1):
        problems.append("presetends: program %d with %d voices sounding after the turn down, program %d and %d notes"
                        " at the end; expected 0, 1, %d, 1" % (f450["patch"], f450["voices0"] + f450["voices1"],
                                                               f["patch"], f["notes"], last))
    lines.append("  PRESETS down from 001: nothing (KEY1 sounds on); up 30: %03d, one program change; up again:"

content.content:
**Supersedes #112** (the owner will close it): the same pin, plus what the firmware suite needs to pass on it.

**What:** `config/fwtest-image` moves to fwtest 0.6.0 (`sha256:8402225f…a116`, as #112). fmgold and fmgold2 now run to 4199 ms instead of 4200, and their golden WAV is the old one less its last 64-frame block. Also M8a's transcript archived, this session's prompt, and the EXPOSURE.md entry.

**Why fmgold came out 128 samples short (the cause):**
- **Not start-up.** `--flash-log` shows no erase or program before 2000.569 ms. The first write is the store's settled save of the selection: a 4 KiB erase plus two page programs, 18 ms busy. One more program follows at 4000.7 ms.
- **What changes.** While the chip is busy, core 0 polls the status register. Blocks 1378 to 1395 carry 48 848 more instructions on core 0; after that, `ipb.csv` matches row for row.
- **Same audio, different end.** The WAV is identical sample for sample over the common length; it just ends where the run ends. A run that ends while core 0 waits ends late (docs/HARNESS.md, "Time"), and the extra instructions put the last run at another phase. The run ended at 4200.406 ms on 0.5.0 and at 4200.243 on 0.6.0. Block 2894 ends at 4200.406, so 0.5.0 got it and 0.6.0 didn't.
- **Why main's `1123eca` passed on 0.6.0** (#112's note): that was phase luck. M8a's code moved the phase.

**Re-record or adjust? Adjusted the case.** At 4200 the run's end sat within 2 µs of a block's end, so any change to core 0's instruction count could flip it again. #126 changes the engine, for one. Re-recording at 4200 would pass only until the next such change. At 4199 the run ends at 4199.24 to 4199.33 ms, about 1.1 ms before the next block ends, which is more than the late ends seen (0.24 to 0.41 ms). No sound changed: the block dropped is silence.

**Result:**
- fmgold at 4199 ms gives the same bytes on 0.5.0 and 0.6.0, and that output is a strict prefix of the old golden.
- Full firmware suite on 0.6.0, locally: **PASS**. Store busy and store wipe: longest save 18.1 ms, 0 underruns.
- CI runs the rest.

**Sources:** none
**Exposure:** firmware side, none (claude-opus-5-5)

**What:** PRESETS no longer wraps from the first program to the last, or from the last back to the first. It stops at the first program (001) and at the last one that holds a patch. A turn past either end does nothing: no program change goes out, no held note is cut, and the operator view's edits are kept, just as a knob turned past its span does nothing. MIDI program changes are unchanged: they select a program directly. Also in this PR: the last clean session's transcript is archived (`7572a4b5`), this session's prompt is saved as `docs/prompts/ARP.md`, and EXPOSURE.md has this session's entry.

**Why:** the owner's answer on #126 (2026-10-25). Wrapping jumps across the test patches, the user slots and (with #126) the presets, which is confusing when playing live.

**Tests and goldens that relied on the wrap:**
- **fmvel** turned PRESETS −1 from 001 to reach test patch 8. It now turns +8.
- **chords** turned PRESETS −3 from 001, with keys held in its columns. It now turns SELECT −3 and PRESETS +3, exactly as #126 has them (`check_chords`, `events/chords.txt`, the 1050 ms LCD golden), so #126 merges this without conflicts there.
- **The store's wear case** turned PRESETS 24 times up from 0 and expected program 24 mod 9. It now turns up to the last test patch, down to the first and up again, so every turn changes the selection.
- **New case `presetends`:** with KEY1 held, PRESETS −2 from 001 does nothing (the note keeps sounding, nothing goes out). +30 stops at 009, with one program change per detent until then. +1 from 009 does nothing.

- DESIGN-NOTES' "Programs" and R-STORE-9 now describe the ends.

- Full firmware suite: every case passes, except midiout's and midilocal's goldens before the re-record (times only).

- C-UNIT: 333 tests OK.

          export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i ~/.ssh/records_key -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes"
          url="[REDACTED:email]:$GITHUB_REPOSITORY.git"
          # Another commit's run may push between our clone and our push:
          # then the push is refused (never forced), and everything is done
          # again on a fresh clone.
          pushed=""
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
            rm -rf rec
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads "$url" records >/dev/null; then
              git clone --quiet --branch records --single-branch "$url" rec
            else
              git init --quiet -b records rec
              git -C rec remote add origin "$url"
            fi
            dest="rec/records/$GITHUB_SHA"
            if [ -e "$dest/report.json" ]; then
              # Never overwrite a record; a re-run is kept beside it. (The
              # folder can exist without one: the audit writes into its audit/.)
              dest="$dest/rerun-$GITHUB_RUN_ID-$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT"
            fi
            mkdir -p "$dest"
            cp -R "out/$GITHUB_SHA/." "$dest/"
            # One line per main commit (and since M4b one per commit and
            # measure in perf-measures.csv); a re-run adds none. A problem
            # with the history must never keep the record from being pushed.
            python tools/perf.py history --record "out/$GITHUB_SHA/report.json" --csv rec/perf-history.csv \
              --measures rec/perf-measures.csv \
              || echo "::error::perf-history.csv or perf-measures.csv: no line appended for $GITHUB_SHA"
            git -C rec add records
            for f in perf-history.csv perf-measures.csv; do
              if [ -e "rec/$f" ]; then git -C rec add "$f"; fi
            done
            git -C rec -c user.name="small-beeps records" -c user.email="records@users.noreply.github.com" \
              commit --quiet -m "records: $GITHUB_SHA" \
              -m "Record of commit $GITHUB_SHA, written by run https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID (attempt $GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT)."
            if git -C rec push --quiet origin records; then
              pushed=1
              break
            fi

## Presets: a bank of our own

- **How many:** 64 presets in 8 categories of 8: keys, bass, bells and
  mallets, brass and winds, pads, leads, plucks and strings, percussion
  and effects. They sit in the image, after the 9 test patches; the 16
  user slots stay as M7 made them.
- **How they are made:** written from scratch in `tools/fm_patch.py`,
  as the test patches are: ratios, levels and envelopes chosen by ear
  and by reasoning (a bell's inharmonic ratios, a bass's short
  modulator decay), each with a line saying what it is for. Never
  derived from anyone's factory sounds: no voice banks or SysEx dumps are
  opened, converted or compared, and no names are borrowed. Each preset's
  history is its commits.
- **How they are tested,** each one in fwtest, by a tool of our own:
  - valid by `fm_patch.problems()`, and all 16 voices sounding within
    the loaded budget;
  - a reference note: no clipping, no DC, no click at note on or off,
    loudness within 3 dB of a target, so the bank plays at one level;
  - its category's shape: a bass has most of its energy below 300 Hz, a
    pad no attack faster than 50 ms, a pluck decays by 30 dB within 2 s;
  - a golden WAV of the reference note, so any change shows;
  - and the owner listens before the bank is merged.

about 348 000 core cycles at 240 MHz. Under the heaviest input, core 0
spends about 110 000 instructions a block (32%), core 1 about 22%, and

# opened, converted or compared, and no names were borrowed. A modulator's
# level L gives an index of about 4 pi x 2^((L - 127) / 8): 127 4 pi, 119
# 2 pi, 111 pi, 103 pi/2, 95 pi/4. Time codes: 2^(t/8) ms over a stage's
# whole range (48 64 ms, 56 128 ms, 64 256 ms, 72 512 ms, 80 1 s, 88 2 s,
# 96 4 s).

              "plucks and strings", "percussion and effects")

        'Tubular': 13,

        if o["level"]:

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
import os
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

fp = load_tool("fm_patch.py")


class FmPatchTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-FM-7"""

    def test_patches_c_is_what_the_tool_writes(self):
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "firmware", "src", "patches.c")) as f:
            self.assertEqual(f.read(), fp.source())

    def test_every_test_patch_is_valid_and_its_own_length(self):
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "firmware", "src", "fm.h")) as f:
            header = f.read()
        self.assertIn("#define FM_PATCHES    %du" % len(fp.TEST_PATCHES), header)
        for p in fp.TEST_PATCHES:
            b = fp.encode(p)
            self.assertEqual(len(b), fp.BYTES)
            self.assertEqual(fp.problems(b), [], p["name"])

    def test_damage_is_refused(self):
        good = bytearray(fp.encode(fp.TEST_PATCHES[1]))
        for at, value in ((0, ord("X")), (2, 2), (3, 111), (16, 0), (16, 11), (17, 8), (18, 2),
                          (29, 1), (fp.OP_OFFSET, 2), (fp.OP_OFFSET + 4, 128), (fp.OP_OFFSET + 5, 8)):
            b = bytearray(good)
            b[at] = value
            s = fp.fletcher16(b[:fp.SUM_OFFSET])
            b[fp.SUM_OFFSET], b[fp.SUM_OFFSET + 1] = s & 0xFF, s >> 8
            self.assertTrue(fp.problems(bytes(b)), (at, value))
        b = bytearray(good)
        b[20] ^= 1                       # a changed byte, the sum left as it was
        self.assertEqual(fp.problems(bytes(b)), ["check sum"])
        self.assertTrue(fp.problems(bytes(good[:100])))

    def test_fletcher16(self):
        # Known values: "abcde" is 0xC8F0, "abcdef" 0x2057.
        self.assertEqual(fp.fletcher16(b"abcde"), 0xC8F0)
        self.assertEqual(fp.fletcher16(b"abcdef"), 0x2057)

    def test_units(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(fp.time_ms(0), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(fp.time_ms(40), 32.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(fp.level_gain(127), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(fp.level_gain(103), 0.125)
        self.assertEqual(fp.level_gain(0), 0.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

### 2026-10-25 ARP: the arpeggiator

Our own design, from docs/ARP-PROPOSAL.md and the owner's answers there
(`firmware/src/arp.c`, `arp.h`; hooks in `fm_play.c`, `fm.c`, `views.c`).

- **What it plays:** while it is on, a note held by a key, by MIDI in or
  by the pedal is the arpeggiator's input, not a note for the engine. It
  plays them one at a time (CHORD: all together) on a clock, each as an
  ordinary note on and off to the engine, so every patch, macro and voice
  rule applies. Its own notes reach the engine past `hold[]`, so a held
  key and the arpeggiator's note of the same pitch never end each other.
- **Modes:** UP and DOWN by pitch; UP/DOWN up then down, the ends not
  repeated; ORDER as the notes came; RANDOM a fixed linear congruential
  generator (x = 1664525 x + 1013904223, the note at (x >> 8) mod the
  count), seeded with 1 each time the arpeggiator starts, so a test can
  predict it; CHORD every note held each step. With 2 to 4 octaves the
  pattern runs through the notes, then again an octave up, and so on
  (CHORD moves the whole chord up an octave a step). A note above 127
  plays octaves lower.
- **Rates:** 1/2, dotted 1/4, 1/4, dotted 1/8, 1/8, 1/8 triplet, dotted
  1/16, 1/16, 1/16 triplet, 1/32: 48, 36, 24, 18, 12, 8, 9, 6, 4 and 3
  MIDI clock pulses (24 a beat), in the owner's order. The grid is whole
  multiples of the step from the clock's zero, so a rate change takes
  effect at the next multiple of the new step, and on MIDI clock the
  steps fall on the sender's beats.
- **Gate and swing:** each note sounds GATE% of its step (10 to 100%),
  ending at the next step at the latest; SWING (0 to 75% in 5% steps)
  delays every odd step of the grid by that share of a step.
- **Latch:** with LATCH on, letting go of the keys keeps the notes
  playing; the first key down after none starts a new chord. Turning
  LATCH off lets go of every note no key holds.
- **Starting and stopping:** a short press of ARP (released within
  500 ms) turns it on or off; held 500 ms, ARP shows its screen instead
  and leaves it as it was. Turned on, the notes held leave the engine
  for the arpeggiator; turned off, every note it played ends and the
  notes held sound again (the panel's only with local control on). On
  the internal clock, the first note held after none starts the pattern
  and the clock at once, so the first note plays at the next block, not
  at the next step; on MIDI clock it waits for the next step.
- **The clock, in exact units:** the clock's position is pulses and
  units of a pulse, 3 750 000 units a pulse. At t beats a minute a frame
  (24 MHz / 544) is 34 t units, exactly (t x 24 / 60 x 544 / 24 000 000
  = 34 t / 3 750 000), so the internal clock never drifts: step k of a
  1/16 at 120 beats a minute is at 5 514.705... frames x k, rounded up to
  the frame, for ever. Only 32-bit divisions are needed (the firmware has
  no 64-bit one).
- **Sample-accurate steps:** each block, before the voices are
  rendered, the clock moves on 64 frames and every step and gate end in
  that span plays at its frame. A start or release at frame f > 0 is
  pending on the voice (`struct fm_voice`'s `pending`, `at`, and for a
  voice still sounding the start's operator values in `next[]`): the
  renderer renders frames 0 to f - 1 as the voice was, takes the start
  or release, then renders f to 63 (`fm.c`, `render_pending`, its own
  copy of the operator loop, so the whole-block path is unchanged). A
  fresh voice is silent before f; a voice taken again (the same note,
  or mono) keeps its phases and starts its attacks from its envelopes'
  levels, as at a block's start. What is not to the frame: a stolen
  voice still fades for a block first (R-FM-4); a release before a start
  on the same voice in one block is dropped (the start wins); and for
  the frames before a start on a voice still sounding, the pitch is
  already the new note's (the pitch is worked out once a block). MIDI
  out sends once a block, so the arpeggiator's notes there are within a
  block and a byte of their frame.
- **MIDI clock (the owner's answer: followed whenever it arrives):**
  - a 0xF8 while on the internal clock starts following it, the position
    taken to the next whole pulse; then each 0xF8 is a pulse, and the
    position never runs more than a pulse past the last clock (so a
    late clock delays the steps, never skips them), and jumps to it if
    it was behind;
  - between clocks the position moves at the rate of the last 24 clocks
    (frames between their arrivals, at the block they were taken), so
    steps between clocks still fall on their frames;
  - Start (0xFA): the next 0xF8 is pulse 0: the pattern and the grid
    start again there. Continue (0xFB): the next 0xF8 carries on from
    where the position is;
  - **when the clock has stopped** (the firmware side's choice, open in
    the proposal): a Stop (0xFC), or 250 ms (172 blocks) without a 0xF8
    while following it. Then the internal clock takes over at once, at
    the settings' TEMPO (not the MIDI clock's last tempo, so what plays
    is what the screen shows), from where the position is: the step
    playing ends at its gate and the next falls where the internal
    tempo puts it. After a Stop, clocks are ignored until a Start or
    Continue (a sender that keeps its clock running while stopped would
    otherwise take it over again). Notes still sounding end at their
    gate.
- **Per patch, per instrument (open in the proposal):** a patch keeps
  on or off, LATCH, MODE, RATE, OCTAVES, GATE and SWING (the patch
  format's version 2, docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md: version 1's three reserved
  bytes, so patches keep their 112 bytes and the store its records'
  sizes). TEMPO and what MIDI out sends belong to the instrument (the
  settings, version 4): changing patch while playing doesn't change the
  tempo, and MIDI out's choice is about what is plugged in. A patch saved
  before ARP (version 1), a preset and every test patch take the
  defaults: off, no latch, UP, one octave, 1/16, no swing, gate 50%. The
  ARP screen's changes are edits of the program, as the operator view's
  are: SAVE keeps them, another program discards them.
- **MIDI out (the owner's answer):** the arpeggiator's notes go out on
  the out channel by default, and the keys held don't; the setting
  (MIDI OUT: keys) sends the keys held instead, and the arpeggiator's
  notes don't. A key's note off goes out only if its note on did, so
  turning the arpeggiator on or off while a key is held leaves no note
  hanging at the far end. With local control off the arpeggiator still
  takes the panel's keys and MIDI in's notes, and its notes go only to
  MIDI out. MIDI clock out is not sent yet (a question for the owner).
- **The screen (ARP held):** the strip shows RATE, MODE, OCTAVES and GATE;
  SELECT pages to SWING, LATCH, TEMPO and MIDI OUT. The body shows the
  settings in words; the info line is its live part (every 50 ms when
  it changes): the clock, internal or MIDI, with its tempo, and the last
  step's note. ARP's LED is lit while the arpeggiator is on, and the
  event line says "ARP on" or "ARP off".
- **Stuck notes:** every note it starts is kept until its gate ends, and
  ends with it, with the pattern stopping, a program or mode change
  (`all_off`), all sound off, or the arpeggiator turned off; each end
  goes to the engine and to MIDI out as its start did.
- **Costs:** off, a block costs it one test (and the ARP button's
  hold check); on, a step is a few hundred instructions, at most 21 a
  second at 1/32 and 240 beats a minute. RAM: about 200 bytes, the
  record 224 bytes, and the voices' pending starts 16 x 332 bytes.
EOF
echo ok

/*
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
 * MIDI out (M6b; docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M6b): a queue of messages, and the
 * transmitter that drains it through UART1's transmit side (HW-72 to
 * HW-74). On the FM-1 the bytes reach no socket (HW-67); in the app they
 * reach other programs.
 * - The engine's block callback (audio.h) is the only writer and the only
 *   reader: midi_out_send() queues a message, midi_out_poll() sends what
 *   waits. Nothing else touches the queue or the UART's transmit side, so
 *   there is no lock and nothing ever waits for the wire.
 * - The transmitter starts a transfer (transmit DMA: TXADR, then TXCNT)
 *   only when the last one has gone (CON0 bit 15, HW-73), never while one
 *   runs, and never changes the bytes of one that runs. A transfer takes
 *   whole messages, up to MIDI_OUT_CHUNK bytes; the poll comes once at
 *   the start of each block and once after the block's events, so a
 *   message queued then has its first byte on the wire at once if the
 *   wire is free.
 * - Running status: a channel message leaves out its status byte when it
 *   is the one sent last, as long as the transmitter has not run dry; the
 *   first message after the queue emptied and the wire went quiet always
 *   carries its status (so a receiver plugged in meanwhile is never left
 *   guessing). System common messages end running status; realtime
 *   messages don't.
 * - When the wire can't keep up (the policy, docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M6b):
 *   a control change, pitch bend, pressure or program change replaces a
 *   waiting one of the same kind, channel (and controller or note), if no
 *   note, mode or other message waits after it; MIDI_OUT_RESERVE places
 *   are kept for note offs (and all notes off, all sound off); any other
 *   message that finds the rest full is dropped and counted. A note off
 *   that finds even the reserve full drops the newest waiting message
 *   that ends no notes instead. A note on dropped either way has its note
 *   off dropped too, so the far end never holds a note it was not sent
 *   and never misses the end of one it was.
 */

#ifndef MIDI_OUT_H
#define MIDI_OUT_H

#include "sb.h"
#include "midi.h"

#define MIDI_OUT_QUEUE   32u   /* messages; at most 96 bytes, 31 ms of the wire */
#define MIDI_OUT_RESERVE 8u    /* of them, kept for note offs */
#define MIDI_OUT_CHUNK   12u   /* the most bytes one transfer takes (3.8 ms) */

/* Queues a message (struct midi_msg, midi.h: a status and 0 to 2 data
 * bytes). Engine callback only. Returns 1 if it was queued or merged with
 * a waiting one, 0 if the policy dropped it. */
int midi_out_send(const struct midi_msg *m);
/* A channel message on the out channel (midi_settings.out_channel). */
int midi_out_channel(u32 kind, u32 d1, u32 d2);
/* Sends what waits, if the wire is free. Engine callback only. */
void midi_out_poll(void);

/* --- The MIDI out record, after MIDI in's (firmware/app.ld) ------------ */
#define MIDI_OUT_MARKER 0x424F444Du   /* "MDOB" in memory order */
struct sb_midi_out_record {
    u32 marker;
    u32 queued;         /* messages queued */
    u32 merged;         /* messages that replaced a waiting one */
    u32 dropped;        /* messages the policy dropped (queue full) */
    u32 offs_dropped;   /* note offs dropped because their note on was */
    u32 offs_lost;      /* note offs dropped: the queue held only note offs */
    u32 waiting_max;    /* the most messages waiting at once */
    u32 messages;       /* messages handed to the wire */
    u32 bytes;          /* bytes handed to the wire */
    u32 running;        /* status bytes left out (running status) */
    u32 transfers;      /* transfers started */
    u32 polls_busy;     /* polls that found a transfer still running */
    u32 thru;           /* messages MIDI thru passed on */
    u32 thru_sysex;     /* System Exclusive messages thru did not pass on */
    u32 panel_notes;    /* note ons the panel sent */
    u32 panel_ccs;      /* control changes the panel's knobs sent */
    u32 panel_programs; /* program changes the panel sent */
    u32 last_note_tick; /* sb_ticks() when the panel's last note on was queued */
    u32 last_start_tick;/* sb_ticks() when the last transfer started */
};
extern volatile struct sb_midi_out_record sb_midi_out;

 *   guessing). System common messages end running status; realtime
 *   messages don't.
 * - When the wire can't keep up (the policy, docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M6b):
 *   a control change, pitch bend, pressure or program change replaces a
 *   waiting one of the same kind, channel (and controller or note), if no
 *   note, mode or other message waits after it; MIDI_OUT_RESERVE places
 *   are kept for note offs (and all notes off, all sound off); any other
 *   message that finds the rest full is dropped and counted. A note off
 *   that finds even the reserve full drops the newest waiting message
 *   that ends no notes instead. A note on dropped either way has its note
 *   off dropped too, so the far end never holds a note it was not sent
 *   and never misses the end of one it was.
 */

#ifndef MIDI_OUT_H
#define MIDI_OUT_H

#include "sb.h"
#include "midi.h"

#define MIDI_OUT_QUEUE   32u   /* messages; at most 96 bytes, 31 ms of the wire */
#define MIDI_OUT_RESERVE 8u    /* of them, kept for note offs */
#define MIDI_OUT_CHUNK   12u   /* the most bytes one transfer takes (3.8 ms) */

/* Queues a message (struct midi_msg, midi.h: a status and 0 to 2 data
 * bytes). Engine callback only. Returns 1 if it was queued or merged with
 * a waiting one, 0 if the policy dropped it. */
int midi_out_send(const struct midi_msg *m);
/* A channel message on the out channel (midi_settings.out_channel). */
int midi_out_channel(u32 kind, u32 d1, u32 d2);
/* Sends what waits, if the wire is free. Engine callback only. */
void midi_out_poll(void);

/* --- The MIDI out record, after MIDI in's (firmware/app.ld) ------------ */
#define MIDI_OUT_MARKER 0x424F444Du   /* "MDOB" in memory order */
struct sb_midi_out_record {
    u32 marker;
    u32 queued;         /* messages queued */
    u32 merged;         /* messages that replaced a waiting one */
    u32 dropped;        /* messages the policy dropped (queue full) */
    u32 offs_dropped;   /* note offs dropped because their note on was */
    u32 offs_lost;      /* note offs dropped: the queue held only note offs */
    u32 waiting_max;    /* the most messages waiting at once */
    u32 messages;       /* messages handed to the wire */
    u32 bytes;          /* bytes handed to the wire */
    u32 running;        /* status bytes left out (running status) */
    u32 transfers;      /* transfers started */
    u32 polls_busy;     /* polls that found a transfer still running */
    u32 thru;           /* messages MIDI thru passed on */
    u32 thru_sysex;     /* System Exclusive messages thru did not pass on */
    u32 panel_notes;    /* note ons the panel sent */
    u32 panel_ccs;      /* control changes the panel's knobs sent */
    u32 panel_programs; /* program changes the panel sent */
    u32 last_note_tick; /* sb_ticks() when the panel's last note on was queued */
    u32 last_start_tick;/* sb_ticks() when the last transfer started */
};
extern volatile struct sb_midi_out_record sb_midi_out;

content.content:
| `--power-cut MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds, then end as a power cut: the flash keeps only the part done of an erase or program in progress, and `flash.bin` is saved ("The flash chip"). In place of `--ms`. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--flash-log` | Save every erase and program the chip started (`flash-ops.csv`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--midi-out` | Save the MIDI output: the bytes with their times (`midi-out.csv`) and the messages they make (`midi-out.txt`). See "MIDI output". |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
